title: Trying to make a teaser trailer for my game, what do you think?
author: cheesyerwin
selftext:
Hello, I am a hobbyist gamedev working on my game, Project SLING, which is a modern re-imagination of a flash game I used to loved and played a lot (Missile Momentum Mayhem), after releasing the new version recently, I was in a state of "development fatigue", so I decided to do something lightweight, then I started typing in prompts on my gemini, and I made this by mixing in some of the game assets, what do you think?

  
btw my game is on [itch.io](http://itch.io)

[https://cheesyerwin.itch.io/project-sling](https://cheesyerwin.itch.io/project-sling)

comments.author: Ohgood9002
comments.body: This does so little to communicate what your game is that it actually makes me want to play it even less

comments.author: Primary-Action825
comments.body: Yeah sorry but the artwork isn’t working for me. I’m pro AI don’t get me wrong, but it’s just too AI if that makes sense

replies.author: cheesyerwin
replies.body: I do argree it is still too AI, I was just trying to experiment so it is kind of expected

replies.author: Primary-Action825
replies.body: That’s the best part is we can now prototype much much faster! Good luck 👍

comments.author: Old-Entertainment844
comments.body: Let me guess: you made the trailerr before the game?

replies.author: cheesyerwin
replies.body: Actually no, as I have said I started messing around after I done with the game

comments.author: Key-Media-6395
comments.body: doesn't really show gameplay or genre, it is a teaser, so that can be expected a little bit, but its probably better to do something that showcases your game more clearly

replies.author: cheesyerwin
replies.body: Yes, that's why I am currently making a second cut with gameplay footage after this teaser

comments.author: Prestigious_Edge_472
comments.body: The trailor art quality aside, what are you hoping this will acheive? I mean when studios do it, it's basically a signal for people who either know the studio and are waiting for the new game release by them, or the next installment in a series (Like when you see a teaser trailor for Diablo 3 when you know Diablo 2, you immediately know what the general concept is even when all you see is the devil in human form doing nothing) but when a 'nameless' indie does it.... you're not telling anyone what your future game is with this, nobody knows who you are or is waiting on your next release, you don't have an established following. I could be wrong, but I don't think this will give you anything, maybe if you incorporate short snippits of the gameplay or mechanics you could capture something with it or raise interest for your game?
